question_text: Government-Owned and Controlled Corporations (GOCCs) are entities owned by the national government. Which of the following best describes their governance structure?

options.text: They are directly managed by the Office of the President without a separate board.
They are governed by a board of directors appointed by the President, with the GOCC's chief executive officer as an ex officio member.
They are autonomous entities with no oversight from any government agency.
They are managed by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) as part of the national budget process.
